props.gloss_en: Reish Lakish's alternative (wheat sown in the ground, eggs under a hen): perhaps R' Shimon does hold muktze where one pushed the thing away with his own hands -- or perhaps there is no difference
R' Yochanan: R' Shimon has muktze only for the oil in a lamp while it burns
since it was set aside for its mitzva, it was set aside for its prohibition
the baraita: one who roofed his sukka properly and adorned it (hangings, fruit, wreaths, wine, oil, flour) may not take from them until the end of the last day of the festival
...and if he stipulated about them, all is according to his stipulation
the sukka-decorations baraita is R' Shimon's
one may not take wood from the sukka on Yom Tov, only from what lies beside it
R' Shimon permits [taking wood from the sukka]
and they agree that the festival sukka, during the festival, is forbidden
...and if he stipulated about it, all is according to his stipulation
we meant [a case] LIKE the oil in a lamp: since it was set aside for its mitzva, it was set aside for its prohibition
R' Yochanan (as R' Chiyya bar Abba reports him): R' Shimon has muktze only in a case like the oil in a burning lamp, since set aside for its mitzva it is set aside for its prohibition

supports.gloss_en: ממאי דרבי שמעון היא? דתני רבי חייא בר יוסף קמיה דרבי יוחנן: ...ושוין בסוכת החג בחג שהיא אסורה -- R' Shimon too forbids what is set aside for the festival's mitzva
איתמר נמי: R' Chiyya bar Abba in R' Yochanan's name -- כעין שמן שבנר

objections.gloss_en: ולית ליה הוקצה למצותו? והתניא: sukka decorations may not be used until the end of the festival -- and that baraita is R' Shimon's (45a.5, from R' Chiyya bar Yosef's baraita): so R' Shimon has muktze for what is set aside for a mitzva alone, not only for the burning oil
